title: Unit economics: warehouse view performance optimizations (partitioning + query plan fixes)
author: Mei Lin
description: This PR improves drilldown query latency for the internal Unit Economics dashboard by tightening warehouse table layout (partitioning/clustering), removing a few high-cost joins and DISTINCTs in the hot path, and switching the most commonly-hit rollups to pre-aggregated/materialized views. The primary goal is to keep p95 query time for time-series + top-N breakdowns under ~2s for typical Finance/Product filter combinations (7d/30d, group_by=model|region|tier) while keeping hourly freshness and correctness intact. Context: during dogfood we saw a few breakdowns regress to 10–25s when grouping by model+region with additional filters (quantization_profile, streaming) due to full scans on hourly fact tables and an inefficient join to the rate card + region mapping tables. This is follow-on work to the initial aggregation job (PR #19342) and API endpoints (PR #19374). Key changes: (1) Re-partition hourly fact + rollup tables by usage_date (derived from usage_hour) and cluster by (canonical_region, customer_tier, model_id) to align with our most common predicates; (2) Introduce a slim dimension table with integer surrogate keys for model_id/region/tier to reduce row width in the largest fact table and avoid repeated string normalization; (3) Replace COUNT(DISTINCT request_id) and per-row JSON extraction in the dashboard views with precomputed columns emitted by the aggregation job; (4) Add/replace two materialized views: unit_econ_rollup_daily_mv (default for 7d/30d) and unit_econ_breakdown_topn_mv (serves top-N tables without scanning the full hourly set); (5) Rewrite the dashboard views to join rate card + allocation factors after aggregation (per hour/day bucket) rather than per request, and to avoid joining region normalization at query time (use canonical_region already stored). Expected impact (measured on staging warehouse with a 14-day slice): time_series(group_by=model, 30d) p95 12.8s -> 1.9s; topN_regions(7d, model=all) p95 8.4s -> 1.3s; drilldown model+region+tier (30d) p95 21.5s -> 2.6s. Notes: No changes to metric definitions; cost attribution math is unchanged. This PR includes a safe migration path: new tables/MVs are built side-by-side, views are swapped, and we keep the prior views for one release behind a feature flag for quick rollback. Backfill/refresh: materialized views refresh hourly; daily MV uses incremental refresh with a 3-day lookback to accommodate late-arriving telemetry.
commits: warehouse: add partition/clustering to unit_econ_hourly_fact and rollups
warehouse: add unit_econ_dim_keys (model/region/tier surrogate ids) + backfill job
views: rewrite unit_econ_dashboard_* views to aggregate before cost joins
perf: remove DISTINCT request_id from dashboard hot path; use precomputed request_count
ops: add query plan notes + EXPLAIN snapshots to /docs for future regressions
testing: Staging validation: (1) Ran 30d dashboard query suite (timeseries + breakdowns) against old vs new views; compared blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens, total_cost_usd, output_tokens across group_bys for exact match within float tolerance (<= 1e-6 on $/1M, exact match on token counts). (2) Verified MV refresh behavior (hourly) and incremental daily MV lookback logic with simulated late-arriving hours. (3) Load test: 50 concurrent dashboard queries for 10 minutes; ensured warehouse credits stayed within expected envelope and p95 latencies met targets. (4) Verified API responses unchanged (schema and ordering), aside from faster response times.
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we confirm clustering choice? model_id is high-ish cardinality; worried about clustering degradation. Also, why both daily MV and topN MV vs a single MV? Mei Lin (author): Agreed on cardinality risk; in staging the clustering benefits still dominate for our access patterns because model_id is heavily filtered/grouped. I also capped clustering keys to 3 and moved quantization_profile out of clustering (kept as a projected column only). Re: two MVs: daily MV serves time series with date predicates; topN MV is keyed to common group_bys and pre-sorts/limits, avoiding scanning all groups for every request. Nadia Rahman (review): The rewrite moves rate card join after aggregation—any risk of shifting allocation when rate_card changes intra-day? Mei Lin: Rate card is versioned by effective_date; we join on usage_date/usage_hour bucket. This is equivalent to prior logic (previously rate card was looked up per request but with the same effective timestamp). Added a regression test covering a rate card boundary day. Chloe Martin (review): Please ensure view swap is gated so Console can roll back quickly if we see discrepancies. Also, what’s the API cache TTL assumption here? Mei Lin: Added feature flag ECON_WAREHOUSE_VIEWS_V2 to choose between old/new views at the query layer (default on in staging, off in prod until rollout). API cache TTL unchanged; this PR just reduces warehouse time so the cache can be shorter if we want later. Allison Grant (review): Any SRE concerns: MV refresh failures, monitoring? Mei Lin: Added two new freshness checks to the existing unit-econ pipeline monitor: MV last_refresh_age_minutes and MV rowcount sanity vs hourly fact. Both wired into the existing alert route. Logan Wright: Request change—document the new “dim_keys” table and rationale; also add an EXPLAIN for the slowest prior query so we have a baseline. Mei Lin: Done in docs/unit-economics/warehouse-performance.md; included before/after plans and the exact query templates used. Approvals: Logan Wright approved after docs update; Chloe Martin approved with the feature-flag gating; Nadia Rahman approved after boundary test; Allison Grant approved after monitoring notes added.
release_notes: Internal-only: unit economics dashboard drilldowns should load significantly faster (esp. 30d + model/region breakdowns). No metric definition changes.
